title: Perdido credits: Persons, Drake, Lenk and Mills
summary: Tizol does not know Persons or Lenk; Ervin Drake wrote the lyrics and Mills was not on Perdido, which was on Tempo.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Juan, we were talking about your compositions, and on Perdido, I found in a discography in the back of the book, Duke Ellington -- His Life and Music, edited by Peter Gamond, a listing of Perdido where it gives composer credit to Tizol and Persons -- and you said you didn't know anybody named Persons?
No, indeed.
And the writer of the lyrics to Perdido was whom?
Oh, that was this one here.
Irwin Drake?
Irwin Drake, yes.
Ervin Drake -- E-r-v-i-n, who is now the President of the American Guild of Authors and Composers, is that correct?
That's right.

And he is the only one who ever wrote lyrics. And then you showed me a 78 record of Woody Herman and the New Third Herd recording of Perdido, and on that record, the composer credits, in addition to yourself and Ervin Drake, lists an H. Lenk. Do you know an H. Lenk? Did he have anything to do with Perdido or the lyrics?
Lenk?
L-e-n-k. That's what it says on that record you showed me.
Well, I don't know. In the beginning, at first, there were two people there on the lyrics. Well, later on, I understand it was only Drake.
Oh. Do you know who the other person was besides him?
No, I don't.
But so far as you know, Drake was the writer.
Yeah.
I see, okay. On 'Perdido', those are the only names I've ever seen on it. I mean, Duke's name has never been on it, Mills' wasn't. I mean, how did you keep Mills' name off that?
Not on 'Perdido'.
Yeah, I know -- so how come Mills didn't get in there on that one?
Well, I don't know about that, because it was on Tempo then.

I see. Oh, that's right -- that was later. And on 'Caravan', it's always said Tizol, Ellington and Mills from the very beginning. And then on 'Conga Brava', which was first recorded in 1940, it was Ellington and Tizol.
